cage. <break time="0.8s" /> And when the attendants poked about in the dirty straw with sticks. <break time="0.8s" /> They found the hunger artist lying there. <break time="0.8s" /> Still fasting. admire it. <break time="0.8s" /> He went on because I have to fast. <break time="0.8s" /> Since I could never find the food I liked. <break time="0.8s" /> And had I found it. <break time="0.8s" /> I would have eaten my fill. <break time="0.8s" /> Like everyone else. <break time="0.8s" /> These were his last words. <break time="0.8s" /> But in his dimming eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> There still remained the firm. <break time="0.8s" /> Though no longer proud. <break time="0.8s" /> Conviction that he was continuing to fast. <break time="0.8s" /> And soon afterward. <break time="0.8s" /> He was quietly buried together with the straw. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the cage. <break time="0.8s" /> They put a young panther. <break time="0.8s" /> Whose noble body. <break time="0.8s" /> Seemed to carry freedom itself in its jaws. <break time="0.8s" /> And the crowds. <break time="0.8s" /> Drawn by its burning joy of life. <break time="0.8s" /> Pressed around the cage. <break time="0.8s" /> And would not move away.
